nodes.statement: Let X be a Hausdorff topological space. A map I colon X to [0,+infty] is called a rate function if it is lower semicontinuous, and a good rate function if it has compact level sets I^-1[0,M] subset X for all M geq 0. \label{thm:caratheodory-vs-hausdorff-convergence}
Suppose that a sequence $(K^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of $\mathbf{D}$-hulls converges to $K \in \Khulls$ in the Carath\'eodory sense and to $\tilde K \in \mathfrak{C}$ in the Hausdorff metric. 
Then, we have 
$\mathbf{D}\smallsetminus K = \component{\mathbf{D}\smallsetminus \tilde K}{\mathfrak{w}}$. 
In particular, we have $K\cap \mathbf{D} = \tilde K\cap \mathbf{D}$ if and only if $\mathbf{D}\smallsetminus \tilde K$ is connected.

The Loewner transform $\LLoewnerTransform[T]$ is a continuous map from $(\funs{T]},\normUniform{\cdot})$ to $\Khulls$ endowed with the Carath\'eodory topology 
(i.e., the topology of uniform convergence on compacts of $\overline{\mathbf{D}}$ as in Lemma~\ref{thm:caratheodory-kernel-convergence}), e.g., by~\cite[Proposition~6.1]{Sheffield-Miller:QLE}.
We can also extend it to infinite time:
\begin{align*}
\LLoewnerTransform \colon \funs{\infty)} \to \Khulls[\infty],
\qquad \LLoewnerTransform(W) := \overline{\underset{T \ge 0}{\bigcup} \, \LLoewnerTransform[T](W)} . 
\end{align*}
For $\mathbf{D} \in \{\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{H}\}$, 
we denote $\LLoewnerTransform[] \in \{\rLoewnerTransform[], \cLoewnerTransform[]\}$, respectively. 

The growing family $(K_t)_{t \ge 0}$ of hulls is said to be \emph{generated by a curve} 
$\gamma \in \Xpathscl$ if $K_t = \filling{\gamma[0,t]}$ for every $t \ge 0$. 
We will be primarily interested in hulls generated by simple curves, 
but we also cautiously note that sequences of 
simple curves in $(\Xpaths,\dXpaths)$ may converge to a curve in $\Xpathscl \smallsetminus \Xpaths$, 
or they may not converge to a curve at all --- even if the hulls generated by them would converge in the Carath\'eodory topology.

Let $(W^{n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be piecewise linear functions converging in $(\funs{T]},\normUniform{\cdot})$ to the driving function $W$ of $\gamma$ as $n \to \infty$, and $K^{n} = \LLoewnerTransform[T](W^{n})$ the corresponding hulls. 
The Loewner transform $\LLoewnerTransform[T] \colon (\funs{T]},\normUniform{\cdot}) \to (\Khulls, \mathcal{T}_{\textnormal{Car}})$ is continuous for the Carath\'eodory topology, 
so we know that the hulls $K^{n}$ converge to $\gamma$ as $n \to \infty$ in the Carath\'eodory sense. 
As $\gamma \in \Xpaths[T]$ is a simple curve, \Cref{thm:caratheodory-vs-hausdorff-convergence} implies that 
$K^{n}$ also converge to $\gamma$ as $n \to \infty$ in the Hausdorff metric, i.e., in $(\mathfrak{C},d_{\mathfrak{C}})$.
Consequently, we have $K^{n} \in U$ for large enough $n$. 
Since the piecewise linear functions $W^{n}$ have finite finite-time Dirichlet energy~\eqref{eq:Dirichlet energy}, 
i.e., $\BMenergy[T](W^{n}) < \infty$ for $T < \infty$, 
we conclude that
\begin{align*}
\Xlenergy[T](U) \; = \;  \inf_{K \in U} \Xlenergy[T](K) 
\; \le \; \Xlenergy[T](K^{n}) \; = \; \BMenergy[T](W^{n}) \; < \; \infty \qquad \textnormal{for large enough } n .
\end{align*}

nodes.statement: This comprises the first two steps in the diagram in Creffig:steps. First, one pushes the finite-time LDP for Brownian motion from Schilder's theorem (Crefthm:Schilders-theorem) via the contraction principle (Crefthm:contraction-principle) to a finite-time LDP for (Xmeasure[T]kappa)_kappa > 0 on Khulls[T] with the Carath\'eodory topology. When kappa le 4, the measures (Xmeasure[T]kappa)_kappa > 0 also restrict to Xpaths[T]. Moreover, as finite-energy curves are simple by Crefthm:finite-energy-is-simple, the restricted measures also satisfy an LDP with the Carath\'eodory topology. Finally, by Crefthm:caratheodory-vs-hausdorff-convergence, on Xpaths[T] the Carath\'eodory topology agrees with that induced by the Hausdorff metric.

This comprises the first two steps in the diagram in \Cref{fig:steps}. 
First, one pushes the finite-time LDP for Brownian motion from Schilder's theorem (\Cref{thm:Schilders-theorem}) 
via the contraction principle (\Cref{thm:contraction-principle}\ref{item:Contraction_principle})
to a finite-time LDP for $(\Xmeasure[T]{\kappa})_{\kappa > 0}$ on $\Khulls[T]$ with the Carath\'eodory topology. 
When $\kappa \le 4$, the measures $(\Xmeasure[T]{\kappa})_{\kappa > 0}$ also restrict to $\Xpaths[T]$.
Moreover, as finite-energy curves are simple by \Cref{thm:finite-energy-is-simple}, 
the restricted measures also satisfy an LDP with the Carath\'eodory topology. 
Finally, by \Cref{thm:caratheodory-vs-hausdorff-convergence}, on $\Xpaths[T]$ the Carath\'eodory topology agrees with that induced by the Hausdorff metric.

Finally, by Crefthm:caratheodory-vs-hausdorff-convergence, on Xpaths[T] the Carath\'eodory topology agrees with that induced by the Hausdorff metric.

\label{thm:chordal-event}
Fix $\beta \in (0,1)$. 
Then, for any $\kappa \in (0, \beta)$ and $\zeta \in \big(0, \frac{1}{2}\big(1-(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2})^{1/2}\big)\big)$ 
there exists $N = N(\beta,\zeta) \in \mathbb{N}$ such that we have
\begin{align*}
\BMmeasure[1]{\kappa}\big[ \funs{1]} \smallsetminus (H(n) \cap L(n)) \big] 
\; \le \; \Big( \frac{n}{2} \Big)^{-\beta/\kappa} \bigg( c_0 + \frac{n}{1-4^{\frac{\beta}{\kappa}-1}} \bigg) ,
\qquad \textnormal{for any } n > N , 
\end{align*}
where $c_0 \in (0,\infty)$ is a universal constant 
\textnormal{(}in particular, independent of $\kappa$, $\beta$, and $n$\textnormal{)},
and the event $\{d_{\!\Hpaths[]}^E(\eta, \eta^n) \le n^{-\zeta}\}$ occurs in the intersection $H(n) \cap L(n)$.

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item Since the map $\lambda \mapsto \hat f_{\lambda, t}$ is continuous (for the locally uniform topology), 
a sequence $(\lambda^{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ converges only if $\hat f_t^{k} := \hat f_{\lambda^{k},t}$ converge to some $\hat f_t$, and since $\hat f_t^{k}$ are conformal maps, by Hurwitz's theorem and the Cauchy formula, 
either the derivatives $(\hat f_t^{k})'$ also converge to $\hat f_t'$, or $\hat f_t' \equiv 0$. 
In either case, if $\lambda^{k} \in L(n)$ for all $k$, then we have
$|\hat f_t'(\mathrm{i} y)| \le \underset{n \to \infty}{\lim} \, |(\hat f^{k}_t)'(\mathrm{i} y)| \le \psi(n) \, y^{-\beta}$ for every $y \in [0, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}} ]$ and $t \in [0,1]$, so $\lambda \in L(n)$.

\item For $\delta < 2/n_1$, set $k(\delta) := \inf\{k\in\mathbb{N} \colon 2/n_k \le \delta\}$. 
Then, for every $\lambda \in H(\vec n)$, the modulus of continuity $\varphi_\lambda$ of $\lambda$ is bounded by $\varphi_\lambda(\delta) \le \varphi(2/n_{k(\delta)}) \xrightarrow{\delta \to 0} 0$. 
This shows that $H(\vec n)$ is a uniformly equicontinuous collection of bounded functions (bounded since $\lambda_0 = 0$). 
By Arzel\`a-Ascoli theorem, we conclude that $H(\vec n)$ is compact.

\item 
Let $\lambda^m \in H(\vec n) \cap L(\vec n)$ be a sequence of drivers converging to $\lambda \in H(\vec n) \cap L(\vec n)$,
and $(\gamma^m)_{m \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $\gamma$ the corresponding hull-generating curves in $\Hpathscl[1]$. 
Then, 
\begin{align} \label{eq:triangle}
d_{\!\Hpaths}^\circ(\gamma, \gamma^m) \le d_{\!\Hpaths[]}^E(\gamma, \eta^{n_k}) + d_{\!\Hpaths}^\circ(\eta^{n_k},\eta^{m,n_k}) + d_{\!\Hpaths[]}^E(\eta^{m,n_k},\gamma^m) , \qquad m,k \in \mathbb{N} ,
\end{align}
where $\eta^{n_k} \in \Hpathscl[1]$ (resp.~$\eta^{m,n_k} \in \Hpathscl[1]$) is the curve driven by the piecewise linear interpolation of 
$\lambda$ (resp.~$\lambda^m$) by equal parts of size $\tfrac{1}{n_k}$ on the interval $[0,1]$: 
\begin{align*}
\lambda_t^{n_k}
:= n_k \big( \lambda_{\ell/n_k}  - \lambda_{(\ell-1)/n_k} \big)
\big( t - \tfrac{\ell-1}{n_k} \big) + \lambda_{(\ell-1)/n_k} , 
\qquad t \in \big[ \tfrac{\ell-1}{n_k}, \tfrac{\ell}{n_k} \big] , \; \ell \in \{1,\ldots,n_k\} ,
\end{align*}
(resp.~$\lambda^{m,n_k}_t := n_k \big( \lambda^m_{\ell/n_k}  - \lambda^m_{(\ell-1)/n_k} \big)
\big( t - \tfrac{\ell-1}{n_k} \big) + \lambda^m_{(\ell-1)/n_k}$). 
On the one hand, in the limit $m \to \infty$, 
the piecewise linear drivers $\lambda^{m,n_k}$ converge to $\lambda^{n_k}$ in $(\funs{1]},\normUniform{\cdot})$, each having finite Dirichlet energy. \begin{align*}
\lim_{m \to \infty} d_{\!\Hpaths}^\circ(\gamma, \gamma^m) \le 2n_k^{-\zeta}

\end{align*}

$(H(\vec n) \cap L(\vec n),\normUniform{\cdot})$ continuously to $(\Hpathscl[1],d_{\!\Hpaths}^\circ)$, 
and also to $(\Hpathscl[1],\dHpaths)$ by \Cref{thm:topology-independent-of-parameterization}.

Finally, fix $M \in [0,\infty)$ and let $n_k = 2\lfloor e^{2Mk-1} \rfloor$. Let $k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ be such that $n_{k_0} > N(\beta,\zeta)$.

\le\;& \sum_{k=k_0}^\infty

\; \le\; ce^{-4(k_0-1)M}e^{-\frac{M}{\kappa}}.
\end{align*}
Increasing the value of $k_0$ if needed 
yields the bound~\eqref{eq:HL_bound} and concludes the proof.

For $\delta < |x|$, consider the stopping time 
$\tilde\tau^x_\delta := \inf\{t \ge 0 \colon |\tilde \bessel^x_t| = \delta\}$ for 
\begin{align*}
\tilde \bessel^x_t = \bessel^x_{t/\kappa}
= x + \int_0^t \frac{a/\kappa}{\bessel^x_s}\,\mathrm{d} s + \int_0^t  \,\mathrm{d} \tilde B_s,
\end{align*}
where $\tilde B_s = \sqrt{\kappa}B_{s/\kappa}$ is a standard Brownian motion. 
Since 
$\BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tilde\tau^x_\delta < \infty] = \big(\delta/|x|\big)^{\frac{2a}{\kappa}-1}$ for all $\kappa < 2a$ 
(see, e.g.,~\cite{Lawler:Conformally_invariant_processes_in_the_plane,Kemppainen:SLE_book, Lawler:SLE_book_draft}), 
we see that choosing $\delta = |x| \, e^{-M/a}$ gives 
\begin{align*}
\BMmeasure{\kappa}\Big[\inf_{t \in [0,\infty)}|\bessel^x_t| \le \delta\Big] \; \le \; \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tilde\tau^x_\delta < \infty] 
\; \le \; e^{-M/\kappa} ,
\qquad \kappa \in (0,a] ,
\end{align*}
which is the claimed inequality.

Fix $M \in [0,\infty)$ and $T = 1$. 
By \Cref{thm:harmonic-measure-is-small-estimate} 
 and \Cref{rem:improvement-of-constant}, 
we find $\delta_n := \delta_{\varepsilon_n}(M,1,1/n) > 0$ for each $t = 1/n$, with $n \in \mathbb{N}$, such that  
\begin{align*}
\BMmeasure{\kappa}\Big[\inf_{s \in [0,1]} \inf_{x \in \mathbb{R} \smallsetminus \{0\}} \min_{u \in [\frac{1}{n},1-s]} |\bessel[s]^x_u| < \delta_n \Big] 
\le 2^{-n} \, e^{-M/\kappa} , \qquad \kappa \in (0,2].
\end{align*}
Set 
\begin{align}\label{eqn:Xset}
X := \bigcap_{n \in \mathbb{N}}
\Big\{\inf_{s \in [0,1]} \inf_{x \in \mathbb{R} \smallsetminus \{0\}} \min_{u \in [\frac{1}{n},1-s]} |\bessel[s]^x_u| \geq \delta_n\Big\} .
\end{align}
Then, $X$ is a closed subset of $\funs{1]}$, and the union bound yields~\eqref{eq:exponentially-tight-function-set}. 


It remains to check that if $\lambda \in X$ and the associated hulls 
$(K_t)_{t \in [0,1]} = (\cLoewnerTransform[t](\lambda|_{[0,t]}))_{t \in [0,1]}$ are generated by a curve $\gamma$, then the curve $\gamma$ is simple. 
If $\gamma$ is not simple, then either (i): $\gamma$ hits $\mathbb{R}\smallsetminus\{0\}$, 
or (ii): there exist times $0 \leq a < b \leq 1$ such that $\gamma(a) = \gamma(b)$. 
In Case~(ii), $\gamma(b) = \gamma(a) \in \gamma[0,s] \subset K_s$ for some $s \in (a, b)$, 
and consequently $x := g_s(\gamma(b)) \in \mathbb{R}\smallsetminus\{0\}$. 
In this scenario, we have $\bessel[s]^x_{b-s} = 0$, 
so there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\frac{1}{n} < b-t$, 
and it follows that $\lambda \notin X$. 
Case~(i) can be regarded as a variant of Case~(ii): 
there exists a time $t > 0$ such that $\gamma(t) \in \mathbb{R}\smallsetminus\{0\}$, 
satisfying the above properties with $s = 0$ and $b = t$. 
Hence, also Case~(i) implies that $\lambda \notin X$. 
This shows that neither Case~(i) nor Case~(ii) is possible.

Note that $\rbessel \sim \pi-\rbessel$ in law. Hence, writing $\delta = \arcsin(\tilde\delta)$, the union bound yields
\begin{align}\label{eqn:sintheta-theta-estimate}
\rDmeasure[T]{\kappa} [\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus S(\tilde\delta)] 
\; \le \; 2 \rDmeasure[T]{\kappa} \Big[\min_{s \in [0,T]}\rbessel_s < \delta\Big] ,
\qquad \tilde\delta \in (0,1) .
\end{align}
Set $q(x) = 2\cot(x) \wedge \frac{1}{x}$, and consider the process $Z = (\Zprocess_t)_{t \ge 0}$ satisfying the SDE
\begin{align}\label{eqn:Zt-SDE}
\,\mathrm{d} \Zprocess_t = q(\Zprocess_t) \,\mathrm{d} t + \sqrt{\kappa} \,\mathrm{d} B_t, \qquad \Zprocess_0 = \tfrac{\pi}{2},
\end{align}
where $\sqrt{\kappa}B$ is the $\BMmeasure{\kappa}$-Brownian motion of~\eqref{eqn:rbessel-SDE}. 
Comparing the SDEs~\eqref{eqn:Zt-SDE} and~\eqref{eqn:rbessel-SDE}, 
we see that as $q(x) \le 2\cot(x)$ for every $x \in (0,\pi)$, 
we have $\Zprocess_t \le \rbessel_t$ for every $t \ge 0$.
Hence, 
\begin{align*}
\rDmeasure[T]{\kappa} \Big[\min_{s \in [0,T]} \Theta_s < \delta\Big] 
\; \le \; \BMmeasure[T]{\kappa}\Big[\min_{s \in [0,T]} \Zprocess_s < \delta\Big] .
\end{align*}
Since $x \cot(x) \to 1$ as $x \to 0$, 
there exists $x_0 > 0$ such that $\frac{1}{x} \le 2\cot(x)$ for every $x \in (0,2 x_0]$. 
In this range, we have $q(x) = \frac{1}{x}$. 
Let $\tau_0 := 0$, and define 
inductively the stopping times
\begin{align*}
\sigma_{n} :=\;& \inf\{s \ge \tau_n \colon \Zprocess_{s} = 2x_0\},\\
\rho_{n} :=\;& \inf\{s \ge \tau_n \colon \Zprocess_{s} = \delta\}, \\
\tau_{n+1} :=\;& \inf\{s \ge \sigma_n \colon \Zprocess_{s} = x_0\} , \qquad n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}.
\end{align*}
Note that for $n \ge 1$, the intervals $(\tau_n, \sigma_n)$ are disjoint 
and $\Zprocess_{\tau_n} = x_0$ is independent of $n$.
Thus, using the strong Markov property, 
we see that the time-shifted processes $\Zprocess[\tau_n]_t := \Zprocess_{\tau_n + t}$ 
are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.), and satisfy the SDE 
\begin{align}\label{eqn:Znt-SDE}
\,\mathrm{d} \Zprocess[\tau_n]_t = \frac{\,\mathrm{d} t}{\Zprocess[\tau_n]_t} + \sqrt{\kappa} \,\mathrm{d} B_{\tau_n + t}, 
\quad t \in [0, \sigma_n-\tau_n] , 
\qquad \textnormal{and} \qquad \Zprocess[\tau_n]_{0} = x_0 .
\end{align}
Note now that $\smash{\underset{s \in [0,T]}{\min} \, \Zprocess_s < \delta}$ can happen 
only if $\rho_n < \sigma_n$ for some $n \ge 1$ for which $\tau_n \le T$. 
We obtain 
\begin{align}
\BMmeasure[T]{\kappa} \Big[\min_{s \in [0,T]} \Zprocess_s < \delta\Big] 
\le\;& \sum_{n = 1}^\infty \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tau_n \le T, \rho_n < \sigma_n] 
&& [\textnormal{monotonicity + union bound}] \nonumber\\
=\;& \sum_{n = 1}^\infty \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tau_n \le T] \; \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tilde \rho_n  < \tilde \sigma_n] 
&& [\textnormal{independence}]\nonumber\\
=\;& \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tilde \rho_1 < \tilde \sigma_1] \sum_{n = 1}^\infty \BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tau_n \le T] ;
&& [(\tilde \rho_n, \tilde \sigma_n) \textnormal{ identically distributed}] 
\label{eqn:min-estimate-helper}
\end{align}
the strong Markov property implies that 
the increments $\tilde \sigma_n := \sigma_n-\tau_n$ and $\tilde \rho_n := \rho_n - \tau_n$ 
are stopping times of $\Zprocess[\tau_n]$ and thus independent of $\tau_n$,
and they are identically distributed.


Next, since the process $\Zprocess[\tau_1]$ up to the stopping time $\tilde \rho_1 \wedge \tilde \sigma_1 \le \sigma_1-\tau_1$ 
satisfies the Bessel SDE~\eqref{eqn:Znt-SDE}, 
by \Cref{thm:harmonic-measure-gets-small-estimate} (with $a=1$),  
we may choose $\delta > 0$ such that 
\begin{align*}
\varlimsup_{\kappa \to 0+} \kappa\log\BMmeasure{\kappa}[\tilde \rho_1 < \tilde \sigma_1] 
= \varlimsup_{\kappa \to 0+}\kappa\log\BMmeasure{\kappa} \Big[\inf_{s \in [0,\tilde \sigma_1]} \Zprocess[\tau_1]_s < \delta \Big] \le -M.
\end{align*}

Fix $M \in [0,\infty)$. 
Using \Cref{thm:radial-harmonic-measure-gets-small-estimate}, 
we fix $\delta = \delta(M) > 0$ such that the bound~\eqref{eq:bound_proba_S} holds for the set $S(\delta)$.
Set $M' = M'(M,T) := M+\frac{3T}{2\delta^2}$. 
Using \Cref{thm:chordal-crad-probability} and \Cref{thm:exponential-tightness-chordal}, 
we can find a time $t = t(M') > 0$ and a compact set $F' \subset \Hpaths[1]$ such that
\begin{align} \label{eq:bound_proba_chord}
\begin{split}
\varlimsup_{\kappa \to 0+}\kappa\log\cHmeasure[1]{\kappa}[\Hpaths[1] \smallsetminus F'] < -M' ,
\\
\varlimsup_{\kappa \to 0+}\kappa\log\cHmeasure[1]{\kappa}[\Hpaths[1] \cap \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1}(\Dpaths[<t])] \le -M' .
\end{split}
\end{align}
By decreasing the value of $t$ if necessary, we may without loss of generality assume 
that $t = T/N$ for some $N \in \mathbb{N}$. 
Recalling the setup of \Cref{thm:chordal-crad-probability}, 
we consider the sets\footnote{\label{fn:proj}Here, we use the notation $\prXpaths{} \in \{\prDpaths{}, \prHpaths{}\}$ for the radial and chordal projection map $\gamma \mapsto \gamma[0,t]$, respectively.}
\begin{align*}
F_0 :=\; & F' \cap \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1}(\Dpaths[\ge t]) \subset \Hpaths[1], 
\\
\tilde{F} := \;& \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(F_0)) = \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(F') \cap \Dpaths[\ge t]) \subset \Dpaths[t], 
 \\
F :=  \; & \Big\{\overset{N}{\underset{j=1}{*}} \gamma_j \;|\; \gamma_j \in \tilde{F} \textnormal{ for all } j\Big\} \subset \Dpaths[T] ,
\end{align*}
where $F$ consists of concatenation of curves in $\tilde{F}$ as in \Cref{app:conformal concatenation}.
We claim that $F$ is a compact subset of $\Dpaths[T]$. 
Indeed, note that the induced map $\gamma \mapsto \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\gamma)$ 
from $(\Hpaths[1],d_{\!\Hpaths}^\circ)$ to $(\Dpaths[<\infty],d_{\Dpaths}^\circ)$ is continuous; 
$(\Dpaths[\ge t],\dDpaths)$ is a closed subset of $(\Dpaths[<\infty],\dDpaths)$;
and the projection $\prDpaths{t} \colon (\Dpaths[\ge t],\dDpaths) \to (\Dpaths[t],\dDpaths)$ is continuous.
Combining these facts with \Cref{thm:topology-independent-of-parameterization}, 
we see that $\tilde{F}$ is a compact subset of $\Dpaths[t]$. 
Hence, we conclude that $F \subset \Dpaths[T]$ is compact as a conformal concatenation of compact sets by \Cref{thm:convergence-of-concatenations} (from \Cref{app:conformal concatenation}).


It remains to estimate $\rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F]$. 
First we bound this probability as follows:
\begin{align*}
\rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F] 
\; \le \; \rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[(\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F) \cap S(\delta)] 
\; + \; \rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus S(\delta)] .
\end{align*}
Using~\eqref{eq:bound_proba_S}, we see that the second term decays exponentially fast with rate $M$ as $\kappa \to 0$. 
Hence, it remains to bound the first term. 
Using \Cref{thm:RN-derivative-radial-chordal} and the choice of $S(\delta)$, we have
\begin{align}
\rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[(\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F) \cap S(\delta)] 
\; \le\; \; & e^{\frac{6-\kappa}{4\kappa} ((\kappa-4)T 
+ T/\delta^2 )} \, \cDmeasure[T]{\kappa} [(\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F) \cap S(\delta)] \nonumber \\
\; \le\;\; & c \, \exp\bigg(\frac{3T}{2\delta^2\kappa}\bigg) \, \cDmeasure[T]{\kappa} [\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F] ,
\label{eqn:exponential-tightness-step}
\end{align}
where $c > 0$ is a constant independent of $\kappa$.
Next, note that we have $\gamma \in \Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F$ if and only if 
$\gamma_j := \hat g_{(j-1)t} (\gamma[(j-1)t, jt]) \notin \tilde F$ for some $j \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, where $\hat g_s(\cdot) := e^{-\mathrm{i} \omega_s} \, g_s(\cdot)$ is the centered radial Loewner map~\eqref{eq:Loewner equation}, 
where $W_s = \omega_s$ is the driving function of $\gamma$.
In particular, by the conformal Markov property of SLE, the union bound yields
\begin{align*}
	\cDmeasure[T]{\kappa} [\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F]
	\; \le \; & N \, \cDmeasure[t]{\kappa} [\Dpaths[t] \smallsetminus \tilde{F}].
\end{align*}
It remains to bound the probability on the right hand side.
For this purpose, we first show the identity${}^{\ref{fn:proj}}$ 
\begin{align}\label{eqn:tildeF}
\tilde F = \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\prHpaths{1}^{-1} F_0)).
\end{align}
Since $F_0 \subset \prHpaths{1}^{-1} F_0$, the inclusion $\tilde F \subset \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\prHpaths{1}^{-1} F_0))$ is clear. 
In order to prove the other inclusion, take $\gamma \in \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\prHpaths{1}^{-1}F_0)$, and let $\eta := (\Phi_{\mathbb{H}} \circ \prHpaths{1} \circ \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1})(\gamma) \in \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(F_0) \subset \Dpaths[\ge t]$. 
Note that since $\gamma \supset \eta \in \Dpaths[\ge t]$, we may project both $\eta$ and $\gamma$ to the time interval $[0,t]$. 
It follows that 
$\prDpaths{t}(\gamma) = \prDpaths{t}(\eta) \in \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(F_0)) = \tilde F$, proving the desired~\eqref{eqn:tildeF}.
We obtain the estimate
\begin{align*}
	\cDmeasure[t]{\kappa}[\Dpaths[t]\smallsetminus \tilde F]
	=\;&  \cDmeasure[t]{\kappa}[\Dpaths[t] \smallsetminus \prDpaths{t}(\Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\prHpaths{1}^{-1} F_0))] 
	&& \textnormal{[by~\eqref{eqn:tildeF}]}
	\\
	\le\;& \cDmeas{\kappa}[\Dpaths \smallsetminus \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}(\prHpaths{1}^{-1}F_0)] 
	&& \textnormal{[as $\cDmeasure[t]{\kappa} = \cDmeas{\kappa}\circ \prDpaths{t}^{-1}$]}
	\\
	=\;& \cHmeasure[1]{\kappa}[\Hpaths[1] \smallsetminus F_0] 
	&& \textnormal{[as $\cHmeasure[1]{\kappa} = \cDmeas{\kappa}\circ \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1} \circ \prHpaths{1}^{-1}$]}
	\\
	\le\;& \cHmeasure[1]{\kappa}[\Hpaths[1] \smallsetminus F'] + \cHmeasure[1]{\kappa}[\Hpaths[1] \smallsetminus \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1}(\Dpaths[\ge 1])] 
	&& \textnormal{[as $F_0 = F' \cup \Phi_{\mathbb{H}}^{-1}(\Dpaths[\ge 1])$]}
\end{align*}
Using~\eqref{eq:bound_proba_chord}, we see that both terms decay exponentially fast with rate $M'$ as $\kappa \to 0$. 
Collecting everything back to \eqref{eqn:exponential-tightness-step} thus yields
\begin{align*}
\varlimsup_{\kappa \to 0+}\kappa\log \rDmeasure[T]{\kappa}[(\Dpaths[T] \smallsetminus F) \cap S(\delta)] 
\; \le \;  \frac{3T}{2\delta^2} - M' = M .
\end{align*}
This concludes the proof.

We prove the claim in the radial case $\Xpaths = \Dpaths$; the chordal case follows similarly.  
Since $\smash{\cev\iota}$ is a continuous bijection, it suffices to show that $\smash{\cev\iota}|_F \colon F \to \cev F := \smash{\cev\iota}(F)$ is an open map. 
For this, let $U \subset \Dpaths[\infty]$ be an open set, take $\gamma \in U\cap F$, 
and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be such that $\Bmetric[{\dDpaths}]{\gamma}{\varepsilon} \subset U$.
Also, take $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\mathrm{diam}\,(\mathbb{D}_n) < \varepsilon$. 
Then, by assumption, there exists an integer $N > n$ such that $\gamma \in \Dpaths[\infty] \smallsetminus \returnevent{n}{N}$. 
Consider the open neighborhood 
\begin{align*}
\smash{\cev\iota}(\gamma) \in \cev V_{\gamma} := \prDpaths{N}^{-1} \big( \Bmetric[\dDpaths]{\gamma[0,N]}{\varepsilon} \big) \subset \smash{\cev{\Dpaths}} .
\end{align*}
Since $\rhittingtime[N](\gamma) \leq N$, we see that for each $\big( \eta[0,t] \big)_{t > 0} \in \cev V_{\gamma} \cap \cev F$, 
we have $\dDpaths(\eta[0,N], \gamma[0,N]) < \varepsilon$, 
and $\gamma[N, \infty) \cup \eta[N, \infty) \subset \mathbb{D}_{n}$.
We thus obtain
\begin{align*}
\dDpaths(\gamma, \eta) \le \max \{ \dDpaths(\eta[0,N], \gamma[0,N]) , \, \mathrm{diam}\,(\mathbb{D}_n) \} < \varepsilon,
\end{align*}
which implies that $\eta \in U$. 
We conclude that $\cev V_{\gamma} \cap \cev F \subset \smash{\cev\iota}(U \cap F)$, 
and consequently, $\smash{\cev\iota}(U\cap F) = \underset{\gamma \in U}{\bigcup} \cev V_{\gamma} \cap \cev F$ is an open set in $\cev F$.
This concludes the proof (of the radial case).

nodes.raw_latex:
Without loss of generality, we work with the space 
$\Xpaths = \Xpaths(\mathbf{D};\mathfrak{z},\mathfrak{w})$ of capacity-parameterized curves in the preferred reference domain $(\mathbf{D};\mathfrak{z},\mathfrak{w})$. 
Fix $M \in [0,\infty)$. 
By \Cref{thm:return-estimates} and \Cref{rem:improvement-of-constant}, there exists $\kappa_0 > 0$ 
and a sequence $\vec N = (N_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of integers with $N_n > n$ (depending on both $n$ and $M$) such that 
\begin{align*}
\SLEmeasure{}{\kappa}[\Xpaths \smallsetminus \xreturnevent{n}{N_n}] \le 2^{-n}e^{-M/\kappa}, \qquad 
\textnormal{for all } \kappa \in (0, \kappa_0) \textnormal{ and } n \in \mathbb{N}.
\end{align*}
By \Cref{thm:limembedding-homeomorphism}, the inverse map $\smash{\cev\iota}^{-1} \colon (\cev F_{\vec N}, \smash{\cev \mathcal{T}_{\dXpaths}}) \to (F_{\vec N}, \dXpaths)$ is continuous on the closed set
\begin{align*}
\cev F_{\vec N} := \smash{\cev\iota} (F_{\vec N}) \subset \smash{\cev{\Xpaths}} , \qquad 
\textnormal{where}
\qquad F_{\vec N} := \bigcap_{n \in \mathbb{N}} (\Xpaths[\infty] \smallsetminus \xreturnevent{n}{N_n}) .
\end{align*}
Furthermore, 
for $\kappa < \kappa_0$ 
the union bound yields${}^{\ref{fn:zeroset}}$
\begin{align*}
\limXmeasure{\kappa}[\smash{\cev{\Xpaths}} \smallsetminus \smash{\cev\iota}(F_{\vec N})]
\; = \; \SLEmeasure{}{\kappa}[\Xpaths \smallsetminus F_{\vec N}]
\; \le \; \sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \SLEmeasure{}{\kappa}[\Xpaths \smallsetminus \xreturnevent{n}{N_n}]
\; \le \; \sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} 2^{-n} e^{-M/\kappa}
\; = \; e^{-M/\kappa},
\end{align*}
so in particular, $\underset{\kappa \to 0}{\varlimsup} \, \kappa\log\SLEmeasure{}{\kappa}[\Xpaths \smallsetminus F_{\vec N}] \le -M$.
We therefore obtain the bounds~\eqref{eq:LDP_bounds} 
by combining 
\Cref{thm:projective-LDP} and the
generalized contraction principle, 
\Cref{thm:contraction-principle-generalized}\ref{item:LDP_gen}.

Recall that a family 
$(A^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of closed sets is \emph{uniformly locally connected} if 
for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exist $\delta = \delta(\varepsilon) > 0$ independent of $n$ such that for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, any two points $x^n, y^n \in A^n$ with $| x^n - y^n | < \delta$ can be joined by a continuum $\varsigma^n \subset A^n$ of diameter $\mathrm{diam}\,(\varsigma^n) < \varepsilon$.

\label{thm:uniform-convergence}
Suppose that $(f^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ are conformal maps from $\mathbb{D}$ onto domains $D^n$ such that $f^n(0)=0$ for all $n$, there exist radii $r,R \in (0,\infty)$ such that 
$\Bmetric[]{0}{r} \subsetneq D^n \subset \Bmetric[]{0}{R}$ for all $n$, 
and the family 
$(\mathbb{C} \smallsetminus D^n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of closed sets is uniformly locally connected. 
Then, if $f^n \to f$ as $n \to \infty$ pointwise on $\mathbb{D}$, 
then the convergence $f^n \to f$ is uniform on $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$.

By \Cref{thm:topology-independent-of-parameterization} it suffices to prove the continuity in the unparameterized metric~$d_{\Xpaths}^\circ$. 
Hence, we aim to prove that for 
any sequences $(\gamma^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(\eta^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converging as $n \to \infty$ respectively to $\gamma$ in $(\Xpaths[<\infty],d_{\Xpaths}^\circ)$ and $\eta$ in $(\overline{\Xpaths}_{<\infty},d_{\Xpaths}^\circ)$,
we also have $\gamma^n * \eta^n \to \gamma * \eta$ in $(\overline{\Xpaths}_{<\infty},d_{\Xpaths}^\circ)$.  
From the definition~\eqref{eqn:concatenation} of the concatenation, we see that
\begin{align}\label{eqn:paths-concat-ineq}
	d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\gamma^n * \eta^n, \gamma * \eta \big) 
	\; \le \; \max\Big(\underbrace{d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\gamma^n, \gamma \big)}_{\underset{n \to \infty}{\longrightarrow} \; 0} ,\; d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\hat f^n_{T^n}(\eta^n), \hat f_T(\eta) \big)\Big) ,
\end{align}
where $(\hat f^n_t)_{t\in [0,T^n]}$ is the centered Loewner map associated to $\gamma \colon [0, T^n] \to \overline {\mathbf{D}}$. 
(Here, we have $\gamma^n \in \Xpaths[T^n]$ for all $n$, and $T^n \to T$ as $n \to \infty$.) 
Note that $\hat f^n_{T^n} \to \hat f_T$ pointwise on $\mathbf{D}$, since $\gamma^n \to \gamma$ in $(\Xpaths[<\infty],d_{\Xpaths}^\circ)$. 
If the convergence $\hat f^n_{T^n} \to \hat f_T$ also holds uniformly 
on the closure $\overline {\mathbf{D}}$, then the second term in~\eqref{eqn:paths-concat-ineq} can be bounded as
\begin{align*}d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\hat f^n_{T^n}(\eta^n), \hat f_T(\eta) \big)
	\; \le \;\; & d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\hat f^n_{T^n}(\eta^n), \hat f_T(\eta^n) \big) + d_{\Xpaths}^\circ \big(\hat f_T(\eta^n), \hat f_T(\eta) \big) 
	\quad \xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{} \quad 0,
\end{align*}
where the first term converges by the uniform convergence of $\smash{\hat f^n_{T_n}} \to \hat f_T$
on $\overline {\mathbf{D}}$, 
and the second term converges since the image of 
the convergent sequence $(\eta^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ under the continuous map $\hat f_T$ converges. 
It thus remains to prove the uniform convergence $\smash{\hat f^n_{T_n}} \to \hat f_T$ on $\overline {\mathbf{D}}$.

\textbf{Radial case, $\mathbf{D} = \mathbb{D}$.} 
Because $\gamma$ is a simple curve, the set $\partial(\mathbb{D} \smallsetminus \gamma[0,t])$ is locally connected for every~$t$, so by~\cite[Theorem~2.1]{Pommerenke:Boundary_behaviour_of_conformal_maps}  
the map $z \mapsto \hat f_t(z)$ has a continuous extension to $\overline{\mathbb{D}} \ni z$ for every~$t$; 
in particular, for $t=T$. 
Because 
$\gamma^n \to \gamma$ in $(\Dpaths[<\infty],d_{\Dpaths}^\circ)$, 
it follows that the boundaries of the slit domains $(\mathbb{D} \smallsetminus \gamma^n[0,t \wedge T^n])_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ are uniformly locally connected.
Hence, by \Cref{thm:uniform-convergence}, we have $\hat f^n_{T^n} \to \hat f_{T}$ uniformly on $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$.


\textbf{Chordal case, $\mathbf{D} = \mathbb{H}$.} 
For each $a \in \mathbb{H}$, we denote by $\varphi_a \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{D}$ the conformal map 
normalized by $\varphi_a(a) = 0$ and $\varphi_a(0) = 1$. 
Note that with $\mathbb{H}$ equipped with the metric $d_{\mathbb{H}}$, 
the function $\varphi_a$ is a bi-Lipschitz map with the bi-Lipschitz constant depending continuously on $d_{\mathbb{H}}(2\mathrm{i}, a)$. 
Since $\gamma[0,T]$ is a bounded set, we can find a point $a_0 \in \mathbb{H}\smallsetminus (\gamma[0,T] \cup \underset{n \in \mathbb{N}}{\bigcup} \, \gamma^n[0,T^n])$.


Write $z := \smash{\hat f_T^{-1}(a_0)}$ and $\smash{z_n := (\hat f^n_{T_n})^{-1}(a_0)}$. 
Note that $z_n \to z$ as $n \to \infty$, 
and consequently, we see that $\varphi_{z_n} \to \varphi_z$ pointwise on $\overline{\mathbb{H}}$. 
Moreover, as the bi-Lipschitz constants of $(\varphi_{z_n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ are uniformly bounded, 
the convergence $\varphi_{z_n} \to \varphi_z$ is actually uniform on $\overline {\mathbb{H}}$. 
Consider now the maps
\begin{align} \label{eq:composed_maps}
\begin{split}
	\tilde f := \; & \varphi_{a_0} \circ \hat f_T \circ \varphi_z^{-1} \;\, \colon \, \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{D} \smallsetminus \varphi_{a_0}(\gamma(0,T]) ,
	 \\
	 \tilde f^n := \; & \varphi_{a_0} \circ \hat f^n_{T_n} \circ \varphi_{z_n}^{-1} \colon \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{D} \smallsetminus \varphi_{a_0}(\gamma^n(0,T^n]).
\end{split}
\end{align}
Now, $\tilde f^n$ converge to $f$ pointwise on $\mathbb{D}$, while the curves $\varphi_{a_0}(\gamma^n)$ converge to $\varphi_{a_0}(\gamma)$ in $(\Dpaths[<\infty],d_{\Dpaths}^\circ)$. 
It thus follows similarly as in the radial case that $\tilde f^n \to \tilde f$ as $n \to \infty$ uniformly on $\overline {\mathbb{D}}$. Finally, since the composed maps in~\eqref{eq:composed_maps} converge uniformly on the closures of their domains, 
$\hat f^n_{T_n} = \varphi_{a_0}^{-1}\circ \tilde f^n \circ \varphi_{z_n}$ 
converge uniformly to $\varphi_{a_0}^{-1} \circ \tilde f \circ \varphi_z = \hat f_T$ on $\overline {\mathbb{H}}$.

\label{rem:convergence-of-concatenations}
Let us demonstrate why the conformal concatenation $(\gamma, \eta) \mapsto \gamma*\eta$  fails to be continuous when 
$\gamma$ is not simple. Consider a crosscut $\gamma \colon [0,1] \to \overline{\mathbb{D}}\smallsetminus\{0\}$ of $\mathbb{D}$ with endpoints $\gamma(0) = 1$ and $\gamma(1) \in \partial\mathbb{D}$, so that $\gamma \in \overline{\Dpaths}_{<\infty} \smallsetminus \Dpaths[<\infty]$.
Fix a point $z_0$ in the interior of $\filling{\gamma[0,1]}$. 
For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, define $\gamma^n \colon [0,1] \to \overline{\mathbb{D}}\smallsetminus\{0\}$ by $\gamma^n(t) := \gamma(\frac{nt}{n+1})$, 
and write $\hat g^n(\cdot) := \hat g_{\gamma^n[0,1]}(\cdot)$ for its centered Loewner map. 
Also, let $\tilde{\eta}^n$ be a simple curve in $\filling{\gamma[0,1]}\smallsetminus \gamma[0, \tfrac{n}{n+1})$ from $\gamma(\tfrac{n}{n+1})$ to $z_0$. 
As the harmonic measure of $\hat\eta^n := \hat g^n(\tilde{\eta}^n)$ vanishes in the limit, 
$\harmonicmeasure{\mathbb{D}}{0}{\hat \eta^n} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, 
the diameter of $\eta^n$ tends to zero as well
--- so in particular $\eta^n$ converges to the constant path $1 \in \Dpaths[0]$ in $(\Dpaths, \dDpaths)$. 
However, by construction, we have $z_0 \in \gamma^n * \eta^n$ for every $n$, while $z_0 \notin \gamma = \gamma * \eta$.
Hence, the convergence of the conformal concatenations $\gamma^n * \eta^n \to \gamma * \eta$ cannot hold in $(\overline{\Dpaths}_{<\infty},\dDpaths)$.

Suppose that the family (P^varepsilon)_varepsilon>0 of probability measures on X satisfies an LDP with rate function I colon X to [0,+infty]. Consider the pushforward probability measures Q^varepsilon := P^varepsiloncirc f^-1 of P^varepsilon by f. Define J colon Y to [0,+infty] by J(y) := I(f^-1\y\) := inf_x in f^-1\y\ I(x) , y in Y . [leftmargin=*, label=textnormal(roman*)] item Suppose that for each M in [0,infty), there exists a closed set E = E(M) subset X only depending on M such that f restricted to E is continuous and varlimsup_varepsilonto 0 varepsilonlog P^varepsilon[X smallsetminus E] le -M. Then, the measures (Q^varepsilon)_varepsilon > 0 satisfy the LDP bounds: we have varliminf_kappa to 0+varepsilonlog Q^varepsilon[G] ge -J(G) textnormaland varlimsup_kappa to 0+varepsilonlog Q^varepsilon[F] le -J(F), for every open G subset Y and closed F subset Y. item If furthermore I is a good rate function and f is continuous on I^-1[0,infty), then also J is a good rate function.

For each M > 0, the set E(M) cap f^-1F is a closed subset of X, so by the union bound and the LDP for (P^varepsilon)_varepsilon>0, we obtain varlimsup_varepsilon to 0varepsilonlog Q^varepsilon[F] \;le\;\;& varlimsup_varepsilon to 0varepsilonlog Big(P^varepsilon[E(M) cap f^-1F] + P^varepsilon[X smallsetminus E(M)]Big)\\ \;le\;\;& - min big\I(E(M) cap f^-1F) , M big\ \;le\; - min big\I(f^-1F) , M big\ \\ xrightarrowM to infty \;& -I(f^-1F) = -J(F). Next, take an open set G subset Y. If J(G) = infty, we trivially have varliminf_varepsilon to 0varepsilonlog Q^varepsilon[G] ge -infty = -J(G). Hence, we may fix M > 0 such that J(G) < M < infty and write E = E(M). As f|_E is continuous, we can find an open set G' subset X such that G' cap E = f^-1G cap E. Now, we have Q^varepsilon(G) \;=\; P^varepsilon[f^-1G] \; ge\; P^varepsilon[G' cap E] \; ge\; P^varepsilon[G'] - P^varepsilon[X smallsetminus E]. We will soon check that I(G') le J(G).
